unresolved_public_documentation_boundari: D1 query table is older than generic Workers subrequest table; their terminology and version differ.
A single D1 batch dispatch can contain several SQL statements; no precise public quota counting rule was found.
No explicit public guarantee that each owner DO RPC resets D1 query/subrequest quotas was found.
If verified on a subsequent publication, acceptance/readback of cpu_ms=300000 would establish configuration capability, not a billing receipt or thousand-expense production acceptance.
CPU time is distinct from wall time. Do not claim configured cpu_ms=300000 gives a DO 900000 ms CPU, or assume a configured global cap is overridden by the Cron default.
excluded_claims: No Paid billing confirmation is inferred from default_usage_model=standard or an unreadable subscription endpoint.
No guarantee is asserted that a separate owner Durable Object invocation resets the D1 query/subrequest quota.
An 800-SQL-statement chunk cap is an independent engineering bound, not a published Cloudflare limit or proof of entitlement.
No source here establishes the final application timeout/concurrency design or thousand-expense native/production acceptance.
